studios.name: Looking Glass Studios
studios.bio: Pioneered first-person immersive simulations with Ultima Underworld, System Shock and Thief, where light, sound and physics let players solve problems their own way. Cash-flow trouble closed the studio in May 2000, scattering its designers across dozens of teams.

diaspora.note: Warren Spector, Harvey Smith and Austin colleagues made Deus Ex and Thief: Deadly Shadows.
Ken Levine, Jonathan Chey and Robert Fermier founded Irrational (System Shock 2, BioShock).
Carried the immersive-sim craft forward with Arx Fatalis, Dishonored and Prey alongside Looking Glass alumni.
Eric Brosius, Terri Brosius and Greg LoPiccolo helped build Frequency, Guitar Hero and Rock Band.
Paul Neurath and Warren Spector reunited years later to revisit Underworld.

studios.name: Bullfrog Productions
studios.bio: Turned Guildford into a British game-making hub with god games and humorous management sims including Populous, Syndicate, Theme Park, Magic Carpet, Theme Hospital and Dungeon Keeper. Acquired by Electronic Arts in 1995 and folded into EA UK by 2001.

diaspora.note: Peter Molyneux, Mark Webley, Tim Rance and Steve Jackson founded Lionhead (Black & White, Fable).
Mike Diskett, Fin McGechie and Guy Simmons left to build Urban Chaos and Startopia.
Bullfrog and Lionhead alumni Mark Healey, Alex Evans, Dave Smith and Kareem Ettouney created LittleBigPlanet.
Theme Hospital veterans Mark Webley and Gary Carr reunited to build Two Point Hospital and Two Point Campus.

studios.name: Westwood Studios
studios.bio: Founded in a Las Vegas garage as Westwood Associates, building Eye of the Beholder, The Legend of Kyrandia, Blade Runner and the real-time strategy template of Dune II and Command & Conquer. Purchased by Electronic Arts in 1998 and liquidated in March 2003.

diaspora.note: Joe Bostic, Michael Legg, Steve Tall and Frank Klepacki stayed in Las Vegas to make Star Wars: Empire at War and Command & Conquer Remastered.
Absorbed Westwood employees who relocated to California for Command & Conquer: Generals and Command & Conquer 3.
Brett Sperry, Adam Isgreen and Rade Stojsavljevic reunited in Las Vegas.

studios.name: Origin Systems
studios.bio: Built under the motto 'We Create Worlds', shaping computer RPGs, space combat and early graphical MMOs through Ultima, Wing Commander, Crusader and Ultima Online. Acquired by Electronic Arts in 1992 and shut down in Austin in February 2004.

diaspora.note: Paul Neurath's Space Rogue relationship with Origin led directly to Ultima Underworld and System Shock.
Chris Roberts, Erin Roberts and Tony Zurovec left in 1996 to make Starlancer and Freelancer.
Warren Spector opened Ion Storm's Austin office with former Origin producers and designers.
Raph Koster and Rich Vogel took their Ultima Online experience straight into Star Wars Galaxies.

studios.name: Sierra On-Line
studios.bio: Started on a Simi Valley kitchen table with Mystery House and grew in the Sierra Nevada foothills into the home of King's Quest, Space Quest, Quest for Glory, Gabriel Knight and Phantasmagoria, while also publishing Half-Life. Cendant accounting fraud, layoffs in 1999 and the 2008 Activision-Vivendi merger ended original development.

diaspora.note: Sister studio in Eugene, Oregon where Jeff Tunnell and Damon Slye built The Incredible Machine, Red Baron and Starsiege: Tribes.
Jane Jensen and composer Robert Holmes continued making narrative mysteries including Moebius.
Lori Ann and Corey Cole returned to adventure-RPG hybrids with Hero-U.
Roberta and Ken Williams came out of retirement to reimagine Colossal Cave in 3D.

studios.name: LucasArts
studios.bio: Founded inside George Lucas's Skywalker Ranch ecosystem as Lucasfilm Games, inventing SCUMM and the no-dead-ends adventure philosophy of Maniac Mansion, The Secret of Monkey Island, Day of the Tentacle and Grim Fandango alongside X-Wing and Dark Forces. Disney shut down internal game development in April 2013, laying off roughly 150 staff.

diaspora.note: Ron Gilbert and Shelley Day left in 1992 to make Putt-Putt, Pajama Sam and Backyard Sports.
Tim Schafer founded Double Fine in San Francisco in 2000 (Psychonauts, Brütal Legend, Broken Age).
Kevin Bruner, Dan Connors and Troy Molander left cancelled Sam & Max sequel work in 2004 to start Telltale.
Lawrence Holland's independent studio built the X-Wing and TIE Fighter flight sims.
Ron Gilbert and Dave Grossman reunited for Thimbleweed Park and Return to Monkey Island.

studios.name: MicroProse
studios.bio: Founded after air-force pilot Bill Stealey met programmer Sid Meier over an arcade cabinet of Red Baron, turning military flight sims into deep historical sandboxes like Pirates!, Railroad Tycoon, Civilization, Darklands and Master of Orion. Debt after Spectrum HoloByte and Hasbro buyouts led Infogrames to close the Hunt Valley studio in 2003.

diaspora.note: Sid Meier, Jeff Briggs and Brian Reynolds left in 1996 to found Firaxis just down the road in Maryland (Alpha Centauri, Civilization III–VII, XCOM).
Civilization co-designer Bruce Shelley joined Tony Goodman in Dallas to help shape Age of Empires.
Brian Reynolds, Tim Train, David Inscore and Jason Coleman founded Big Huge Games in 2000 (Rise of Nations).

studios.name: Clover Studio
studios.bio: Established by Capcom as a semi-autonomous team dedicated to original worlds rather than sequels, shipping Viewtiful Joe 2, the ink-painted adventure Okami and the slapstick brawler God Hand in under three years. Capcom dissolved the studio in March 2007 after its three core leads resigned to stay independent.

diaspora.note: Atsushi Inaba, Hideki Kamiya and Shinji Mikami formed Seeds Inc., merging with ODD to become PlatinumGames (Bayonetta, Vanquish, NieR: Automata).
Shinji Mikami later founded Tango Gameworks in Tokyo in 2010.
Hideki Kamiya opened CLOVERS in 2024 and partnered with Capcom to direct an Okami sequel.

studios.name: Pandemic Studios
studios.bio: Spun out of Activision veterans to make open-ended action and combined-arms games including Battlezone II, Full Spectrum Warrior, Star Wars: Battlefront I & II, Destroy All Humans!, Mercenaries and WWII stealth sandbox The Saboteur. Electronic Arts bought the studio in 2007 and shut it down in November 2009.

diaspora.note: Several Pandemic designers and engineers moved to Microsoft's Halo team.
Los Angeles neighbors at Respawn hired former Pandemic developers on Titanfall and Star Wars Jedi.
Greg Borrud and Chris Miller co-founded Seismic Games in Los Angeles.

studios.name: Volition
studios.bio: Founded in Champaign as Parallax Software for six-degrees-of-freedom shooter Descent before becoming Volition in 1996 and building FreeSpace, Red Faction's Geo-Mod destruction and the Saints Row open-world comedies. Embracer Group closed the 30-year studio in August 2023 during corporate cost cuts.

diaspora.note: Co-founder Matt Toschlog split amicably in 1996 to open Outrage in Ann Arbor (Descent 3).
Veterans Matt Madigan, Brian Traficante and Rob Loftus founded Shapeshifter in Champaign in 2024, co-developing Clockwork Revolution with inXile.

studios.name: Visceral Games
studios.bio: Grew from EA Redwood Shores' licensed action teams (James Bond, The Lord of the Rings) into the studio behind Dead Space, where diegetic HUDs and limb-cutting turned sci-fi survival horror tactile. Electronic Arts closed Visceral in October 2017 while cancelling Amy Hennig's single-player Star Wars project.

diaspora.note: Glen Schofield and Michael Condrey left in 2009 to found Sledgehammer (Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, WWII).
Schofield and Dead Space alumni later built The Callisto Protocol.
Dead Space creative director Bret Robbins founded Ascendant to ship Immortals of Aveum.
EA's Montreal studio rebuilt Dead Space (2023) in consultation with fans and series veterans.

studios.name: Tango Gameworks
studios.bio: Founded by Shinji Mikami to mentor younger directors in Tokyo, producing The Evil Within, Ghostwire: Tokyo and John Johanas's rhythm-action hit Hi-Fi Rush. Microsoft abruptly shut the studio in May 2024, before Krafton stepped in that August to acquire the Hi-Fi Rush rights and rehire roughly half the staff to reopen Tango in Tokyo.

diaspora.note: Art and creative director Ikumi Nakamura founded Tokyo indie studio Unseen in 2022 (Kemuri).
Shinji Mikami left Tango in 2023 and established Kamuy to back smaller, faster-cycle teams.

studios.name: Arkane Austin
studios.bio: Opened in Texas by Arkane founder Raphaël Colantonio to tap Austin's Looking Glass and Ion Storm heritage, co-developing Dishonored with Arkane Lyon before leading the Talos I immersive sim Prey (2017) and co-op shooter Redfall. Microsoft closed the Austin studio in May 2024 alongside Tango Gameworks.

diaspora.note: Raphaël Colantonio and executive producer Julien Roby left in 2017 and founded WolfEye in 2019 (Weird West).
Sister studio Arkane Lyon continues operating in France on Dishonored, Deathloop and Marvel's Blade.

studios.name: Lionhead Studios
studios.bio: Named after Mark Webley's hamster after breaking away from EA-owned Bullfrog, creating creature-AI god game Black & White, studio sim The Movies and the fairytale RPG trilogy Fable. Acquired by Microsoft in 2006 and closed in April 2016 following the cancellation of live-service spin-off Fable Legends.

diaspora.note: Mark Healey, Alex Evans, Dave Smith and Kareem Ettouney left Lionhead in 2006 to make LittleBigPlanet and Dreams.
Sean Murray and colleagues from Guildford's Lionhead/Criterion circle founded Hello Games (Joe Danger, No Man's Sky).
Co-founder Mark Webley teamed up with Gary Carr to launch Two Point Hospital.
Took up the Fable mantle in Leamington Spa, hiring several former Lionhead developers.

studios.name: Ensemble Studios
studios.bio: Combined MicroProse's historical sweep with Warcraft's real-time controls to create Age of Empires, Age of Mythology and console RTS Halo Wars. Microsoft bought Ensemble in 2001 and closed it in January 2009 right as Halo Wars wrapped.

diaspora.note: Co-founder Rick Goodman left after Age of Empires I to make Empire Earth.
Co-founder Brian Sullivan left after Age of Empires II to create Titan Quest.
Tony Goodman and dozens of Ensemble staff immediately formed Robot Entertainment in Plano (Orcs Must Die!, Age of Empires Online).
Ensemble veterans later joined Zynga Dallas, Boss Fight Entertainment and other North Texas studios.

studios.name: Troika Games
studios.bio: Named for the Russian word for a trio after Fallout creators Tim Cain, Leonard Boyarsky and Jason Anderson left Interplay in 1998. In seven years they shipped three deep, reactive RPGs—Arcanum, The Temple of Elemental Evil and Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines—before closing in February 2005 when publisher funding dried up.

diaspora.note: Tim Cain and Leonard Boyarsky eventually reunited at Obsidian to direct The Outer Worlds.
Leonard Boyarsky spent a decade at Blizzard as lead world designer on Diablo III.
Bloodlines writer Brian Mitsoda founded DoubleBear to make Dead State.
Jason Anderson and Chad Moore contributed to Wasteland 2 and Clockwork Revolution.

studios.name: Black Isle Studios
studios.bio: Grew out of Brian Fargo's Interplay RPG heritage (The Bard's Tale, Wasteland, Fallout) into Feargus Urquhart's internal RPG division, developing Fallout 2, Planescape: Torment and Icewind Dale while publishing BioWare's Baldur's Gate. Parent company Interplay laid off the entire Black Isle staff in December 2003, cancelling their original Fallout 3 ('Van Buren').

diaspora.note: Fallout leads Tim Cain, Leonard Boyarsky and Jason Anderson departed in 1998 to form Troika.
Feargus Urquhart, Chris Avellone, Chris Parker, Darren Monahan and Chris Jones founded Obsidian in 2003, later making Fallout: New Vegas.
Interplay founder Brian Fargo launched inXile in 2002 (Wasteland 2 & 3, Torment: Tides of Numenera).

studios.name: Blizzard North
studios.bio: Founded in the Bay Area as Condor before Blizzard acquired it nine months prior to shipping Diablo in 1996, turning roguelike dungeon crawls into fast mouse-driven action RPGs with Diablo and Diablo II. Vivendi conflicts prompted its founders to walk out in 2003, and Blizzard shuttered the San Mateo office in August 2005.

diaspora.note: Blizzard and Battle.net engineers Mike O'Brien, Patrick Wyatt and Jeff Strain left in 2000 to build Guild Wars.
Brevik, the Schaefers and Bill Roper founded Flagship in 2003 (Hellgate: London).
Max Schaefer, Erich Schaefer, Travis Baldree and composer Matt Uelmen created Torchlight I & II.
Erich Schaefer, Phil Shenk and Peter Hu teamed up again to reimagine action RPGs.

studios.name: Irrational Games
studios.bio: Founded near Boston by three Looking Glass veterans, building System Shock 2, Freedom Force, SWAT 4, the underwater dystopia of BioShock and BioShock Infinite. In February 2014 Ken Levine wound down the large studio—laying off all but 15 staff—before reorganizing that small core as Ghost Story Games in 2017.

diaspora.note: Ken Levine and 15 Irrational colleagues formed a small narrative team inside Take-Two to build Judas.
BioShock 2: Minerva's Den leads Steve Gaynor, Johnnemann Nordhagen and Karla Zimonja founded Fullbright (Gone Home, Tacoma).
BioShock Infinite veterans Forrest Dowling, Gwen Frey and Damian Isla built The Flame in the Flood.
Jordan Thomas and Stephen Alexander formed Question (The Magic Circle, The Blackout Club).

studios.name: Ion Storm
studios.bio: Started in a glass penthouse in Dallas by id Software co-founders John Romero and Tom Hall (Daikatana, Anachronox), while Warren Spector's quieter Austin branch shipped cyberpunk immersive sim Deus Ex and Thief: Deadly Shadows. Owner Eidos closed Dallas in 2001 and shut down Austin in February 2005.

diaspora.note: Warren Spector founded Junction Point in Austin (Epic Mickey).
Harvey Smith and several Deus Ex and Thief designers joined Raphaël Colantonio on Dishonored and Prey.
John Romero and Tom Hall formed a small mobile and handheld team in Texas in 2001.
Revived the Deus Ex and Thief series in Quebec with Deus Ex: Human Revolution.

studios.name: Free Radical Design
studios.bio: Founded in Nottingham by GoldenEye 007 and Perfect Dark leads who left Rare to make the fast, split-screen TimeSplitters trilogy and psychic stealth game Second Sight. Administration in 2008 turned the studio into Crytek UK and later Dambuster Studios; a 2021 TimeSplitters reformation under Deep Silver was shut down by Embracer in December 2023.

diaspora.note: Nottingham successor studio formed from Crytek UK staff in 2014, later shipping Dead Island 2.
Origin studio where the founders first built GoldenEye 007 before striking out on their own.

studios.name: Bizarre Creations
studios.bio: Founded in Liverpool by Martyn Chudley as Raising Hell Software before adopting Bizarre Creations in 1994, pairing precision driving with style points ('Kudos') across Formula 1, Metropolis Street Racer, Project Gotham Racing and Blur, plus twin-stick hit Geometry Wars. Activision bought the studio in 2007 and closed it in February 2011.

diaspora.note: Recruited Bizarre Creations, Codemasters and Criterion driving veterans in Leamington Spa to build Forza Horizon.
Pete Wallace, Craig Howard and Liverpool colleagues immediately formed Lucid Games in 2011.
Ben Ward, Stephen Cakebread and Peter Collier formed a small indie studio after the shutdown.

studios.name: Psygnosis
studios.bio: Born from the ashes of Liverpool's Imagine Software under Roger Dean's owl logo, publishing Amiga landmarks Shadow of the Beast and Lemmings before helping define PlayStation's club-culture identity with WipEout, Destruction Derby and Colony Wars. Sony renamed it Studio Liverpool in 2000 and closed it in August 2012 after 28 years.

diaspora.note: Graeme Ankers, Lee Carus, Chris Roberts, Stuart Tilley and Stuart Lovegrove kept the Liverpool team spirit alive by founding Firesprite in 2012 (later acquired by Sony).
WipEout co-creator Nick Burcombe founded Playrise Digital in 2012 (Table Top Racing).
Former Psygnosis veterans built futuristic anti-gravity racer Pacer.

studios.name: Japan Studio
studios.bio: Sony's oldest internal game studio in Tokyo backed offbeat, auteur-driven experiments from Ape Escape, LocoRoco, Patapon, Echochrome and Gravity Rush to Team Ico's Ico and Shadow of the Colossus, while co-producing Demon's Souls and Bloodborne with FromSoftware. Sony wound down most of Japan Studio in April 2021, folding remaining hardware-play staff into Team Asobi.

diaspora.note: Nicolas Doucet's internal Astro Bot group spun out as a standalone PlayStation studio in Tokyo, winning Game of the Year with Astro Bot (2024).
Fumito Ueda and Team Ico colleagues formed independent studio genDESIGN in 2014, completing The Last Guardian.
Silent Hill, Siren and Gravity Rush creator Keiichiro Toyama left in 2020 with Kazunobu Sato and Junya Okura to make Slitterhead.

studios.name: Team Bondi
studios.bio: Founded in Sydney by The Getaway director Brendan McNamara, spending seven years building 1947 Los Angeles and full-performance facial capture for detective thriller L.A. Noire. Exhausting crunch, unpaid-credit disputes and debt pushed the studio into liquidation in October 2011 just months after L.A. Noire topped charts.

diaspora.note: George Miller's Sydney production house absorbed much of the staff before cancelling Whore of the Orient.
Brendan McNamara opened Video Games Deluxe in Sydney in 2013 for L.A. Noire: The VR Case Files; Rockstar acquired it in March 2025 as Rockstar Australia.

studios.name: United Front Games
studios.bio: Formed in Vancouver by open-world and racing veterans from EA Black Box, Radical Entertainment and Rockstar Vancouver, shipping kart-creator ModNation Racers and rescuing Activision's cancelled True Crime: Hong Kong with Square Enix to release martial-arts crime drama Sleeping Dogs. Abruptly closed its doors in October 2016.

diaspora.note: Sleeping Dogs design director Mike Skupa and Vancouver colleagues founded boutique horror studio Brass Token (The Chant).
Many Vancouver engineers and artists moved across town to Microsoft's Gears of War team and Klei Entertainment.

studios.name: Midway
aliases: Vid Kidz (Eugene Jarvis and Larry DeMar) / Williams
Eugene Jarvis & Larry DeMar (Vid Kidz / Williams)
studios.bio: Anchored Chicago's coin-op arcade scene alongside corporate sibling Williams Electronics, licensing Space Invaders and Pac-Man in America before creating Defender, Robotron: 2084, Joust, Spy Hunter, Rampage, Smash TV, Mortal Kombat and NBA Jam. Struggled with the transition away from arcades and liquidated in Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2009.

diaspora.note: Warner Bros. bought the Chicago Mortal Kombat team under Ed Boon in 2009, rebranding it NetherRealm Studios (Mortal Kombat 9–1, Injustice).
Defender and Cruis'n creator Eugene Jarvis founded arcade maker Raw Thrills outside Chicago in 2001.
Chicago studio led by Dave Lang that hired numerous Midway veterans.

studios.name: Hudson Soft
studios.bio: Founded in Sapporo by brothers Yuji and Hiroshi Kudo as an amateur-radio and microcomputer shop, becoming the first third-party Famicom licensee, co-designing the PC Engine (TurboGrafx-16) with NEC, and creating Bomberman, Star Soldier, Adventure Island, Military Madness and Mario Party 1–8. Absorbed into Konami in March 2012, retiring the Hudson name.

diaspora.note: Nintendo's Sapporo/Tokyo party-game subsidiary hired core Hudson Mario Party staff led by Hidetoshi Endo, continuing Super Mario Party.
Absorbed remaining Hudson staff and took over Bomberman and Momotaro Dentetsu.

studios.name: AlphaDream
studios.bio: Founded in Tokyo by former Square president Tetsuo Mizuno with Super Mario RPG co-director Chihiro Fujioka and Yoshihiko Maekawa, turning slapstick pixel animation and timed button presses into the handheld Mario & Luigi RPG series. Rising 3D development costs and sluggish late-era 3DS remake sales forced bankruptcy in October 2019.

diaspora.note: Longtime Mario & Luigi writer/director Hiroyuki Kubota and several colleagues moved to Nintendo's Monolith Soft.
Partnered with Nintendo and returning AlphaDream veterans including Yoshihiko Maekawa to revive the series with Mario & Luigi: Brothership (2024).

studios.name: Cing
studios.bio: Founded in Fukuoka by former Riverhillsoft producer Takuya Miyagawa and scenario writer Rika Suzuki, crafting rotoscoped, novel-like Nintendo DS mysteries held sideways like a paperback—Another Code (Trace Memory), Hotel Dusk: Room 215 and Last Window—plus co-developing Little King's Story. Filed for bankruptcy in March 2010.

diaspora.note: Co-founder Rika Suzuki continued writing mystery scenarios and visual novels through Bellwood Inc.
Acquired Cing's library and reunited artist/director Taisuke Kanasaki on Chase: Cold Case Investigations and Nintendo's Another Code: Recollection (2024).

studios.name: Neversoft
studios.bio: Started by three Malibu Interactive refugees in Los Angeles, rescuing the Apocalypse engine to build Spider-Man (2000) and the combo-chaining skateboarding phenomenon of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1–4, Tony Hawk's Underground, Western shooter Gun and Guitar Hero III. Activision folded Neversoft into Infinity Ward in July 2014, where staff burned a giant eyeball effigy in the parking lot.

diaspora.note: Absorbed the remaining Woodland Hills team directly into Call of Duty development.
Rebuilt Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2 in 2020 with reverence for Neversoft's original physics code before also being merged into Blizzard.

studios.name: Maxis
studios.bio: Co-founded by Will Wright and Jeff Braun when no publisher wanted a city builder with no win state, shipping SimCity, SimEarth, SimAnt, SimCity 2000, dollhouse life sim The Sims and evolutionary sandbox Spore. Electronic Arts bought Maxis in 1997 and shuttered the original Emeryville flagship studio in March 2015 after SimCity (2013), keeping the Maxis label for The Sims teams elsewhere.

diaspora.note: Will Wright left in 2009 to run an experimental toy and game lab, later co-founding Gallium Studios.
Lead designer Stone Librande took his tabletop-first prototyping workshops from Emeryville to Riot.

studios.name: Ultimate Play the Game
studios.bio: Founded in a Leicestershire townhouse by arcade-conversion veterans Tim and Chris Stamper, pushing the 48K ZX Spectrum with Jetpac, Atic Atac, Sabre Wulf and the isometric Filmation 3D rooms of Knight Lore. Realizing British 8-bit tape sales were peaking while the NES rose abroad, the Stampers wound down original Ultimate development in 1985 to form Rare.

diaspora.note: Tim and Chris Stamper moved down the road to Twycross manor to reverse-engineer the NES and build Rare into a console powerhouse.

studios.name: DMA Design
studios.bio: Started in a Dundee computer club by student David Jones, shipping Amiga shooters Menace and Blood Money before Mike Dailly's tiny animated sprites sparked Lemmings, followed by Body Harvest, Space Station Silicon Valley, Grand Theft Auto and Grand Theft Auto III. After Take-Two acquired the studio, Dundee closed and the Edinburgh team was renamed Rockstar North in 2002.

diaspora.note: DMA's Edinburgh team became Rockstar North directly after Grand Theft Auto III, making Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV and GTA V.
Founder David Jones stayed in Dundee to form Realtime Worlds in 2002, creating open-world superhero sandbox Crackdown and APB.
Chris van der Kuyl and Paddy Burns helped turn Dundee into a console-port hub known for Minecraft Console Edition.

studios.name: Rockstar North
studios.bio: Formed when DMA Design's Edinburgh studio took the Rockstar North name in 2002, turning Grand Theft Auto III's streaming 3D city tech into Vice City, San Andreas, Manhunt, Grand Theft Auto IV and Grand Theft Auto V while co-developing Red Dead Redemption 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI.

diaspora.note: Longtime Rockstar North president and producer Leslie Benzies founded Build A Rocket Boy in Edinburgh.
Works as flagship production partner across Rockstar's international studio network.

studios.name: Rockstar Games
studios.bio: Established in New York in December 1998 inside Take-Two by Sam and Dan Houser, uniting DMA Design in Scotland with Diego Angel's Angel Studios in California (Midtown Madness, Midnight Club, Red Dead Redemption) and Barking Dog in Vancouver (Bully) into a single global development network on Red Dead Redemption 2.

diaspora.note: Co-founder and lead writer Dan Houser left in 2020 and launched Absurd Ventures with longtime audio/radio collaborator Lazlow Jones and Michael Unsworth.

studios.name: DICE
studios.bio: Started in a Växjö dorm room by Amiga demoscene group The Silents (Pinball Dreams), merging with Stockholm's Refraction Games in 2000 to create 64-player combined-arms shooter Battlefield 1942, first-person parkour runner Mirror's Edge and the Frostbite engine. Acquired by Electronic Arts in 2006, with generations of Stockholm departures seeding new Swedish studios.

diaspora.note: Patrick Söderlund, Stefan Strandberg, Johan Andersson and DICE veterans left to found Embark in Stockholm in 2018 (The Finals, ARC Raiders).
Battlefield: Bad Company 2 lead designer David Goldfarb and Ben Cousins formed The Outsiders in Stockholm (Metal: Hellsinger).
Longtime 'Mr. Battlefield' creative director Lars Gustavsson and DICE colleagues formed Time To Kill Games in 2023.

studios.name: Embark Studios
studios.bio: Founded in Stockholm in November 2018 by former DICE and EA technical and creative leads looking to build systemic multiplayer worlds with smaller, faster procedural pipelines. Shipped server-side structural destruction shooter The Finals (2023) and retro-futuristic machine-scavenging extraction shooter ARC Raiders (2025).

studios.name: Nintendo
studios.bio: Founded in Kyoto as a handmade hanafuda card workshop before maintenance engineer Gunpei Yokoi's 'lateral thinking with withered technology' and young industrial artist Shigeru Miyamoto reshaped video games across Donkey Kong, Super Mario, The Legend of Zelda, Metroid, Animal Crossing and Splatoon. Internal R&D divisions (R&D1–4, later EAD and SPD) consolidated into Nintendo EPD in 2015.

diaspora.note: Game Boy and Metroid producer Gunpei Yokoi left in 1996 to found Koto, designing Bandai's WonderSwan handheld before his death in 1997.
Former Konami and Nintendo collaborators led by Etsunobu Ebisu partnered closely with Kyoto producers on Kirby's Epic Yarn and Yoshi's Crafted World.

studios.name: Capcom
studios.bio: Founded in Osaka by Kenzo Tsujimoto ('Capsule Computers'), forging frame-tight arcade action in Ghosts 'n Goblins, Mega Man and Street Fighter II before defining survival horror with Resident Evil, stylish action with Devil May Cry, courtroom drama with Ace Attorney and co-op hunting with Monster Hunter.

diaspora.note: Internal Osaka studio spun up for Viewtiful Joe, Okami and God Hand, whose leads went on to found PlatinumGames and Tango Gameworks.
Street Fighter co-creators Takashi Nishiyama and Hiroshi Matsumoto founded Dimps in Osaka, later co-developing Street Fighter IV.
Street Fighter II planner Akira Nishitani left in 1995 to form Arika (Street Fighter EX, Tetris: The Grand Master).
Producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi and later Dragon's Dogma / Devil May Cry director Hideaki Itsuno moved to new Osaka/Tokyo studios in the 2020s.

studios.name: Konami
studios.bio: Began as an Osaka jukebox repair business before building 1980s–2000s arcade and console staples including Frogger, Gradius, Castlevania, Contra, Suikoden, Beatmania, Pro Evolution Soccer, Team Silent's Silent Hill and Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear. Corporate shifts toward mobile and pachislot in the 2010s drove a major wave of senior creators to form independent studios.

diaspora.note: Masato Maegawa and frustrated Konami programmers left in 1992 to make original action games starting with Gunstar Heroes, Radiant Silvergun and Ikaruga.
Hideo Kojima and Yoji Shinkawa re-established Kojima Productions independently in December 2015 after Metal Gear Solid V.
Castlevania: Symphony of the Night producer/writer Koji Igarashi left in 2014 to crowdfund Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.
Late Suikoden creator Yoshitaka Murayama reunited Suikoden veterans to build Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes.

studios.name: Sega
studios.bio: Grew from Tokyo coin-op distributor Service Games into an arcade and console powerhouse organized into fiercely competitive internal teams: Yu Suzuki's AM2 (Out Run, Virtua Fighter, Daytona USA, Shenmue), Sonic Team (Sonic the Hedgehog, NiGHTS, Phantasy Star Online), AM3/Hitmaker (Sega Rally, Crazy Taxi), UGA (Rez) and RGG Studio (Yakuza / Like a Dragon). Exited console hardware after the Dreamcast in 2001.

diaspora.note: Sega Rally and Rez producer Tetsuya Mizuguchi left in 2003 to make Lumines, Child of Eden and Tetris Effect.
AM2 pioneer Yu Suzuki founded Ys Net in Tokyo in 2008, later directing Shenmue III.
Super Monkey Ball and Yakuza creator Toshihiro Nagoshi left in 2021 to start Nagoshi Studio in Shibuya.

studios.name: Namco
studios.bio: Started by Masaya Nakamura with two mechanical rocking horses on a Yokohama department-store roof, ushering in color arcade character design with Galaxian, Pac-Man, Dig Dug, Xevious and The Tower of Druaga before leading 3D arcade hardware with Ridge Racer, Tekken, Soulcalibur, Ace Combat and Katamari Damacy. Merged with Bandai in 2005–2006.

diaspora.note: Xevious and Tower of Druaga creator Masanobu Endo founded independent Tokyo developer Game Studio in 1985.
Virtua Fighter and Tekken designer Seiichi Ishii left to found DreamFactory (Tobal No. 1, Ehrgeiz).
Tetsuya Takahashi and Hirohide Sugiura founded Monolith Soft (Xenosaga, Xenoblade) with Namco capital in 1999 before Nintendo acquired it in 2007.
Katamari Damacy creator Keita Takahashi went independent (Wattam, To a T).

studios.name: Atari
aliases: Atari (Nolan Bushnell, Steve Bristow, Steve Wozniak)
studios.bio: Kickstarted commercial video games in Sunnyvale with Pong, Breakout, Asteroids, Centipede, Missile Command, Tempest, Star Raiders and the Atari 2600, before Warner split consumer hardware from coin-op division Atari Games (Marble Madness, Gauntlet, Paperboy) in 1984. Warner's refusal to credit or pay royalties to programmers sparked the industry's first third-party studio walkouts.

diaspora.note: Atari 2600 programmers David Crane, Larry Kaplan, Alan Miller and Bob Whitehead walked out in 1979 to become the first third-party publisher and put developer names on boxes.
Rob Fulop, Dennis Koble, Bill Grubb and Bob Smith followed suit in 1981 (Demon Attack, Cosmic Ark).
Several early Atari computer designers, including Ozark Softscape's Dani Bunten and Star Raiders programmer Doug Neubauer, published milestone work beyond Atari.

studios.name: id Software
studios.bio: Formed in Shreveport, Louisiana by four coworkers borrowing Softdisk PCs after hours to write smooth side-scrolling Commander Keen, then moving to Texas to build Wolfenstein 3D, Doom and Quake while open-sourcing their engines for modders and rival studios alike. Joined ZeniMax in 2009 and reinvented fast arena combat in Doom (2016) and Doom Eternal.

diaspora.note: Creative director Tom Hall left during Doom to make Rise of the Triad and guide Terminal Velocity and Prey.
John Romero and Tom Hall reunited in Dallas in 1996 to found Ion Storm.
Brenda Romero and John Romero founded independent studio Romero Games in Galway, Ireland in 2015.

studios.name: Valve
aliases: Day of Defeat team (mod), later Valve
studios.bio: Founded by former Microsoft engineers Gabe Newell and Mike Harrington, licensing id's Quake engine to build seamless first-person storytelling in Half-Life, then hiring student modders and DigiPen graduates to ship Counter-Strike, Team Fortress 2, Portal, Left 4 Dead, Dota 2 and Half-Life: Alyx alongside PC storefront Steam and the Steam Deck.

diaspora.note: Portal lead designer Kim Swift left in 2009 to direct Quantum Conundrum before later leading teams at Motive and Xbox.
Late Half-Life 2 art director Viktor Antonov shaped the industrial visual architecture of Dishonored in Lyon.
Left 4 Dead writer Chet Faliszek and Kimberly Voll founded co-op studio Stray Bombay (The Anacrusis).

studios.name: Blizzard Entertainment
studios.bio: Founded in Irvine by three UCLA graduates as Silicon & Synapse (The Lost Vikings, Rock n' Roll Racing) before polishing real-time strategy, MMOs, card battlers and hero shooters in Warcraft, StarCraft, World of Warcraft, Hearthstone and Overwatch. Decades of ownership changes through Vivendi, Activision and Microsoft (2023) prompted wave after wave of spin-off studios across Orange County.

diaspora.note: Mike O'Brien, Patrick Wyatt and Jeff Strain left in 2000 to create Guild Wars in Bellevue.
Didier Malenfant left Blizzard with Naughty Dog alumni Ru Weerasuriya and Andrea Pessino in 2003 (Daxter, The Order: 1886).
Hearthstone director Ben Brode and Hamilton Chu left in 2018 to build Marvel Snap.
Co-founder Mike Morhaime launched Dreamhaven (Moonshot Games, Secret Door) in Irvine in 2020 with longtime Blizzard leads.
StarCraft II and Warcraft III veterans Tim Morten and Tim Campbell left in 2020 to keep real-time strategy alive with Stormgate.

studios.name: FromSoftware
studios.bio: Spent eight years writing agricultural and business software in Tokyo before shipping PlayStation launch dungeon crawler King's Field (1994) and mech builder Armored Core (1997). Former Oracle account manager Hidetaka Miyazaki joined at 29, took over a struggling fantasy prototype called Demon's Souls, and led the studio through Dark Souls, Bloodborne, Sekiro and Elden Ring.

studios.name: Square Enix
studios.bio: Unites two foundational Japanese RPG lineages that merged in April 2003: Enix (founded 1975, home of Yuji Horii, Akira Toriyama and Koichi Sugiyama's Dragon Quest) and Square (founded 1986, home of Final Fantasy, Chrono Trigger, Secret of Mana, Xenogears and Kingdom Hearts), later rebuilt online around Naoki Yoshida's Final Fantasy XIV turnaround.

diaspora.note: Xenogears director Tetsuya Takahashi and Soraya Saga left Square in 1999 to build Xenosaga and Xenoblade Chronicles.
Former Square president Tetsuo Mizuno and Super Mario RPG veterans founded AlphaDream in 2000.
Final Fantasy creator Hironobu Sakaguchi founded Mistwalker in 2004 after The Spirits Within (Blue Dragon, Lost Odyssey, Fantasian).
Mana creator Koichi Ishii opened Grezzo in 2006 (Ever Oasis, Zelda remakes, Echoes of Wisdom).

studios.name: BioWare
studios.bio: Founded in Edmonton by newly graduated medical doctors Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, reviving party-based computer RPGs with the Infinity Engine on Baldur's Gate I & II before building Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Jade Empire, Mass Effect and Dragon Age. Acquired by Electronic Arts in 2007.

diaspora.note: Co-founder Trent Oster and Cameron Tofer formed Beamdog in Edmonton in 2009 to restore Baldur's Gate, Planescape: Torment and Neverwinter Nights.
BioWare Austin veterans Arnie Jorgensen, Alex Thomas and John Watson left to make tactical trilogy The Banner Saga.
Baldur's Gate and KOTOR creative leads James Ohlen, Chad Robertson and Drew Karpyshyn reunited in Austin on sci-fi RPG Exodus.
Dragon Age creator and lead writer David Gaider co-founded Summerfall in Melbourne (Stray Gods).

studios.name: Bethesda Game Studios
studios.bio: Founded by Christopher Weaver as Bethesda Softworks (Gridiron!, Wayne Gretzky Hockey) before Julian LeFay and Ted Peterson created first-person open-world RPGs Arena and Daggerfall, and Todd Howard and Ken Rolston bet the studio's survival on hand-crafted Morrowind (2002). Followed with Oblivion, Fallout 3, Skyrim, Fallout 4 and Starfield; acquired by Microsoft in 2021.

diaspora.note: Arena and Daggerfall architects Ted Peterson, Julian LeFay and Vijay Lakshman reunited in 2019 to build spiritual successor The Wayward Realms.
Fallout 3/4/76 project lead Jeff Gardiner and Skyrim/Fallout artist Nate Purkeypile left to start indie teams (Wyrdsong, Just Purkey Games).

studios.name: Obsidian Entertainment
studios.bio: Founded in an attic office in June 2003 as Black Isle Studios collapsed at Interplay, building reactive RPG sequels Knights of the Old Republic II, Neverwinter Nights 2 and the 18-month desert political drama of Fallout: New Vegas. Saved itself from near-closure in 2012 through the Pillars of Eternity Kickstarter, later shipping Grounded, Pentiment, The Outer Worlds and Avowed under Xbox.

studios.name: Arkane Studios
studios.bio: Founded in Lyon in October 1999 by former Electronic Arts France staffer Raphaël Colantonio out of admiration for Ultima Underworld, making subterranean RPG Arx Fatalis, physics brawler Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, clockwork stealth series Dishonored and time-loop assassination puzzle Deathloop. While sister branch Arkane Austin was closed in 2024, Arkane Lyon continues in France.

diaspora.note: Founder Raphaël Colantonio and Julien Roby formed WolfEye Studios in 2019 to make smaller systemic RPGs starting with Weird West.

studios.name: Larian Studios
studios.bio: Named after founder Swen Vincke's dog Lar, surviving nearly two decades of publisher cancellations and contract work on Divine Divinity and Divinity II before betting the studio on self-published, systemic co-op RPGs Divinity: Original Sin I & II and scaling across seven international studios to ship Baldur's Gate 3 (2023).

studios.name: CD Projekt Red
studios.bio: Grew out of Marcin Iwiński and Michał Kiciński's Warsaw PC localization company (which translated Baldur's Gate into Polish with full local voice acting), opening a Łódź and Warsaw development team in 2002 to adapt Andrzej Sapkowski's Witcher novels into The Witcher trilogy and Mike Pondsmith's tabletop RPG into Cyberpunk 2077.

diaspora.note: Former CD Projekt and Metropolis Software colleagues Grzegorz Miechowski, Przemysław Marszał and Michał Drozdowski founded 11 bit in Warsaw (This War of Mine, Frostpunk).
Witcher 2 & 3 veteran Jakub Rokosz founded Fool's Theory in Bielsko-Biała (The Thaumaturge, The Witcher Remake).
Witcher 3 game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz and quest director Mateusz Tomaszkiewicz formed Rebel Wolves in Warsaw (The Blood of Dawnwalker).
Cyberpunk 2077 and Witcher veterans Mateusz Kanik, Jędrzej Mróz and Marcin Jefimow launched Blank. in Warsaw in 2023.

studios.name: Remedy Entertainment
studios.bio: Started in a house basement in Espoo by members of Finnish PC demoscene group Future Crew (Death Rally), bringing literature student Sam Lake aboard to write and lend his own grimacing face to bullet-time noir shooter Max Payne, followed by weird-fiction connected universe games Alan Wake, Quantum Break, Control and Alan Wake 2.

diaspora.note: Remedy's benchmark tool 3DMark spun out into sister hardware-testing company Futuremark in 1997.
Co-founder Petri Järvilehto later co-founded Helsinki mobile studio Seriously (Best Fiends).

studios.name: Housemarque
studios.bio: Finland's oldest still-active game studio, formed in 1995 when Amiga shoot-'em-up pioneers Bloodhouse (Stardust) and Terramarque (Elfmania) merged in Helsinki. Kept pure arcade bullet-curtain design alive through Super Stardust HD, Resogun and Nex Machina (co-designed with Eugene Jarvis) before translating that craft into third-person roguelike Returnal and Saros.

studios.name: Hazelight Studios
studios.bio: Founded in Stockholm in 2014 by Lebanese-Swedish film director Josef Fares and core Starbreeze Studios colleagues after making Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons, dedicating the studio solely to split-screen and Friend's Pass co-op adventures where mechanics change every chapter: A Way Out, It Takes Two and Split Fiction.

studios.name: Supergiant Games
studios.bio: Started in the living room of Amir Rao's father's San Jose house after Rao and Gavin Simon left EA Los Angeles following Command & Conquer 3, recording Bastion's acoustic soundtrack and narration in a bedroom closet. Across Bastion, Transistor, Pyre, Hades and Hades II, the roughly 25-person team has kept mandatory vacation, no crunch and almost zero staff turnover.

studios.name: Team Cherry
studios.bio: Grew out of 2013 Ludum Dare game jam prototype Hungry Knight in Adelaide, where animator Ari Gibson and designer William Pellen raised AU$57,000 on Kickstarter to hand-draw the vast subterranean insect kingdom of Hollow Knight (2017) and its seven-year follow-up Hollow Knight: Silksong (2025) as a tiny three-to-four-person studio.

studios.name: Kojima Productions
studios.bio: First created inside Konami in 2005 for Metal Gear Solid 4, Peace Walker, hallway horror teaser P.T. and Metal Gear Solid V, then dissolved during Hideo Kojima's 2015 split with Konami and immediately reborn that December as an independent Tokyo studio with character artist Yoji Shinkawa. Partnered with Guerrilla Games on the Decima engine to ship asynchronous traversal dramas Death Stranding and Death Stranding 2.

studios.name: Rare
studios.bio: Evolved directly out of Ultimate Play the Game on a Leicestershire manor farm after the Stamper brothers reverse-engineered the NES, delivering Battletoads, Donkey Kong Country, Killer Instinct, GoldenEye 007, Banjo-Kazooie, Perfect Dark and Conker's Bad Fur Day for Nintendo before Microsoft bought Rare in 2002 (Viva Piñata, Sea of Thieves).

diaspora.note: GoldenEye 007 and Perfect Dark leads David Doak, Steve Ellis, Karl Hilton and Graeme Norgate left in 1999 to make TimeSplitters in Nottingham.
GoldenEye 007 director Martin Hollis founded Zoonami in Cambridge in 2000.
Banjo-Kazooie and Donkey Kong Country veterans Gavin Price, Chris Sutherland, Steve Mayles and Grant Kirkhope reunited near Twycross for Yooka-Laylee.

studios.name: Bungie
studios.bio: Started in a Chicago apartment by University of Chicago undergrads Alex Seropian and Jason Jones, shipping Mac sci-fi shooter Marathon and real-time tactics game Myth before Microsoft acquired the team in 2000 to turn Halo: Combat Evolved into the dual-stick template for console FPS games. Bought back its independence in 2007, launched shared-world shooter Destiny and joined Sony in 2022.

diaspora.note: Co-founder Alex Seropian left in 2002 to start Wideload in Chicago (Stubbs the Zombie) and later Industrial Toys.
Halo 2 multiplayer lead Max Hoberman founded Certain Affinity in Austin in 2006.
Took over Halo stewardship at Microsoft in 2007 alongside several Bungie alumni.
Marty O'Donnell, Jaime Griesemer and Jared Noftle formed Highwire in Seattle.

studios.name: Naughty Dog
studios.bio: Founded in Virginia by 14-year-old high-school friends Andy Gavin and Jason Rubin as JAM Software before moving to Universal's backlot in California to squeeze Crash Bandicoot onto the original PlayStation, followed by Jak and Daxter, Amy Hennig's pulp adventure Uncharted and Bruce Straley and Neil Druckmann's The Last of Us. Joined Sony in 2001.

diaspora.note: Uncharted 1–3 creative director and writer Amy Hennig leads narrative adventures at Skydance (Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra).
Uncharted 2/4 and The Last of Us game director Bruce Straley returned to games in 2022 to found indie team Wildflower.

studios.name: Insomniac Games
studios.bio: Founded in Burbank by Ted Price and brothers Alex and Brian Hastings right next door to longtime friends and engine-sharing neighbors Naughty Dog, building Spyro the Dragon, gadget platformer Ratchet & Clank, Resistance, Sunset Overdrive and Marvel's Spider-Man across three decades before joining PlayStation Studios in 2019.
